newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares up as investors in buying mood.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares up as investors in buying mood.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose slightly on Thursday as investors made the most of low prices to buy up lucrative stock, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority's (CMA) all-share index rose 1.15 points to close at 397.86 from 396.71 on Wednesday in low turnover of 62.20 million pounds ($18.32 million).
"It was a good trade today. People are buying because of low prices," said broker Mohammed Magdi of EFG/Hermes brokerage.
Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN was the day's most active stock, trading in almost 9.00 million pounds but it ended the day 0.50 pounds lower at 124.5, the CMAdaily report said.
"There was very high demand for PACHIN today. It seems an investor who bought lots of shares during the recent flotation is selling them and people are buying because of the good price," Madgi said.
He said reports the govenment plans to sell 30 percent of the stock through a Global Depositry Offer had encouraged buyers.

The milling sector in general performed well, with North Cairo Flour Mills in second position on the day's top 10 list of most active shares. It rose 2.00 pounds to close at 184 after trading in more than 4.40 million pounds.
"Prices in the milling sector went down too low recently and this has boosted trade in that sector," Magdi said.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills closed 4.98 pounds higher at 104.74 after more than 3.78 million pounds changed hands.
East Delta Flour Mills rose 3.61 pounds to 82.75 after trading in almost 3.00 million pounds and Upper Egypt Flour Mills traded in more than 2.95 million pounds and closed 3.9 pounds higher at 88.00.
The cement sector ended unchanged or fractionally higher but traded actively, with Amriyah Cement leading the way. Amriyah traded in more than 4.36 million pounds and closed 0.49 higher at 86.99.

Helwan Portland Cement ended unchanged at 80 pounds but traded in more than 2.50 million pounds, while Egyptian Tora Portland Cement rose 0.7 pounds to close at 96.2 after more than 2.00 million pounds changed hands.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 653.22 from 651.57 points on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 264.99 from 264.17.
Out of the 81 shares traded, 39 gained, 25 lost and 17 ended the day unchanged.
